evidence: checks.json reports patch_applies: true for run-08.

Diffing base against generated shows exactly the 11 files listed in patch.diff: CHANGELOG.md, docs/reference/tabs.md, sandbox/tabs_demo.css, sandbox/tabs_demo.py, src/textual/renderables/opacity.py, src/textual/renderables/underline_bar.py, src/textual/widgets/tabs.py, tests/renderables/test_opacity.py, tests/renderables/test_underline_bar.py, tests/test_tabs.py. The generated tree also has a harness .git directory, which is not part of the patch.

No tests were run, per the experiment setup. Candidate test expectations were traced by reading (for example test_tabs.py fixed-padding row " Home  Files " and test_underline_bar action list) and appear consistent with the candidate code.
Tabs and Tab are in src/textual/widgets/tabs.py, the same path as reference.diff.
UnderlineBar changes are in src/textual/renderables/underline_bar.py and Opacity changes in src/textual/renderables/opacity.py, matching the reference.
docs/reference/tabs.md ("::: textual.widgets.tabs.Tabs") matches the reference page.

Tabs.__init__ parameters (tabs.py:262-276) match reference tabs.py:199-212 by name and default, plus an added name parameter. Tab(label, name=None) matches the reference dataclass constructor (reference tabs.py:24-39).
UnderlineBar gains clickable_ranges with default None (underline_bar.py:29,35). It is typed Mapping rather than the reference's dict, which is compatible.
action_range_clicked(name) exists at tabs.py:384, matching reference tabs.py:311.

Deviation: find_tab_by_name returns the LAST index for duplicate names (tabs.py:311-332, docstring at :322). The reference returns the FIRST (reference tabs.py:325-331, docstring 'Return the index of the first tab with a certain name').
Deviation: tabs.py:179-219 renders every tab, including duplicates. The reference's dict (reference tabs.py:62) keeps only the final duplicate, as documented at reference tabs.py:31.
criteria.deficiency: Public method find_tab_by_name returns a different index than the reference for duplicate tab names (last vs first), and duplicate-named tabs are rendered differently. Signatures and types otherwise match. Impact is limited to the duplicate-name case.

evidence: tabs.py:3-19 imports stdlib, rich, and the package modules .. events, .._layout_resolve, ..keys, ..reactive, ..renderables.opacity, ..renderables.underline_bar, and ..widget. These are all lower-level or peer modules.
underline_bar.py:1-6 and opacity.py:1-8 import only stdlib, rich, and textual.renderables, so no reverse dependency is introduced.
widgets/__init__.py in base does not export any widget that needs registration, and the reference does not add Tabs there either, so no registration is required.
Click dispatch uses the existing mechanism: the @click meta range_clicked('name') is routed to action_range_clicked (tabs.py:384) through base dispatch_action (app.py:621-630).
docs/reference/tabs.md is added, matching the reference.
tabs.py imports only stdlib (math, dataclasses, typing), rich (cells, console, segment, style, text), and textual internals.
rich is already pinned in pyproject.toml (rich ^11.2.0) and poetry.lock (version 11.2.0). No new dependency is added.
Label and bar layout lives in the renderable TabsRenderable (tabs.py:58-220), which mirrors the reference split (reference tabs.py:45-171).
Widget state, reactive properties, and key handling live in Tabs (tabs.py:221+), as in the reference (reference tabs.py:174+).
Click ranges are passed to UnderlineBar as generic clickable_ranges (underline_bar.py:97-135, :138), which matches the reference design.

Minor: _TabEdge (tabs.py:41) is a private dataclass that duplicates the layout Edge concept instead of changing _layout_resolve. Base Edge is a Protocol, so this is an acceptable duck-typed alternative.
Reuses layout_resolve (tabs.py:14, used at :150), Opacity (tabs.py:17), and UnderlineBar (tabs.py:18) instead of creating parallel mechanisms.
Click handling goes through the existing @click meta and action_* dispatch (tabs.py:384; app.py:621).
Animation uses the existing self.animate and reactive watch_* mechanism (tabs.py:395).
The Opacity fix keeps segment metadata by merging style + blended color (opacity.py:36-45). This is a renderable-level concern and does not leak widget state.
The Tabs widget owns state and keys (tabs.py:221+), and the renderables only receive plain data (tabs list, indices, styles, ranges).
UnderlineBar takes generic clickable_ranges and knows nothing about tabs (underline_bar.py:29,35,97-135).

Handlers are async, matching base conventions: async on_key (widget.py:356; _scroll_view.py:152), async watch_* (_header.py:47; _scroll_view.py:82), and the awaited async app.set_focus (app.py:306; tabs.py:428).
Docstrings use the Google Args style used across base modules.
Relative imports inside the widgets package match _header.py.
sandbox/tabs_demo.py:on_key mirrors the sandbox/local_styles.py:19-20 pattern.
Minor, not a failure: the action string is built with !r (tabs.py:192; underline_bar.py:113). The reference uses literal quotes. Both give range_clicked('name') for ordinary names.

Tab padding is not styled with the tab background. tabs.py:189-199 and :218 emit padding with padding_style = None for the active tab or a meta-only Style for inactive tabs, so padding cells lose the tab background. The reference builds padded_label including padding (reference tabs.py:115-120) and styles the whole string (:120 active, :122-127 inactive). rich/text.py:160 defines __str__ and no __format__, so the reference's padding spaces are plain text that take the tab style.

Empty-tabs layout differs. tabs.py:103-110 returns the underline without a leading Segment.line(), placing the bar on row 1. The reference always yields Segment.line() (reference tabs.py:86-89), placing the bar on row 2 of the height-2 widget. The candidate's test_tabs.py empty-tabs test encodes its version.
Duplicate names are handled differently (see api_contract): the candidate renders all duplicates (tabs.py:179-219) and picks the last index (tabs.py:311-332).

Deliberate and not held against the candidate: tab_padding=0 means zero padding (tabs.py:128-133). The reference's 'tab_padding or None' (reference tabs.py:96) makes 0 flexible, which contradicts its 'fixed' docstring.
Keyboard and mouse behavior matches the reference: left/right wrap, digits with 0 meaning 10th or last, first-character search, escape, and click via range_clicked.
criteria.deficiency: Visible rendering differs from the reference in two ways. First, tab padding does not carry the tab background, so tabs look narrower with gaps. Second, with no tabs the underline is drawn on the first row instead of the second. Duplicate-name behavior also differs. Core keyboard and click behavior is intact.
